rv.q: This show’s sheer joyful energy is enough to carry the audience through a patchy but very, very funny story of two ordinary lads with a big goal in sight.
The mayhem of Eastlake’s prediction is endearing – but to come alive properly, it needs a steadier pulse.
But the script as a whole is messy and incohesive, its various parts pulling away from each other.
Sadly, it’s a case of bigger not always being better and the piece feeling bloated rather than effectively expanded.

cn.t: This Geordie football musical about two teens chasing Newcastle United season tickets earns praise for its infectious energy and underdog spirit, but critics find the storytelling unfocused and uneven despite its remarkable journey from 60-seat venue to West End.
